name: @wellsfargo-starui/apps
description: Consumer/reference apps for @wellsfargo-starui. Two tracks: source/ resolves @wellsfargo-starui/* out of the platform checkout, tarball/ installs the packed bucket tarballs the way an external team would. Never deployed.
//platform-link: The platform checkout is located at install time by scripts/resolvePlatform.mjs (STARUI_PLATFORM env, else a sibling directory, else a scan) — no directory name is hardcoded here. preinstall vendors its packed tarballs for the tarball track; postinstall symlinks node_modules/@wellsfargo-starui/platform for the source track.
//workspaces-note: tarball/* is deliberately NOT a workspace. Its file: deps point at tarball/.vendor/*.tgz, which scripts/setup.mjs creates — and npm resolves the workspace tree BEFORE running any root lifecycle script, so a workspace member can never depend on files an install-time hook produces. Installing it separately is also higher fidelity: an external consumer has its own isolated node_modules, not this repo's hoisted one. Use `npm run setup:tarball`.

scripts.setup:tarball: node scripts/setup.mjs && node scripts/makeTarballApp.mjs --all && node scripts/installTarball.mjs
scripts.build: npm run build:source && npm run build:tarball
scripts.typecheck: npm run typecheck:source && npm run typecheck:tarball
scripts.test:all: node scripts/app-track.mjs test source && node scripts/app-track.mjs test tarball

//types-note: React types live at the repo root so every app — and the package .d.ts they pull in — sees exactly one copy. Two @types/react in one graph produce spurious JSX type conflicts.
